why:
Drops `release-event` from _buildReleaseEventLi()'s
  • . That class is the ONLY thing _findCellReleaseEventParts() scopes on, and it is exactly what the old bespoke `
  • XX date
    • ` lacked — so the 'Release events - Country' and '- Date' sections disappear again. The original main defect.

name: the country span loses its native release-country class
why: Both `_findCellCountryNameParts()` and ColumnDataExtractor.splitCountryDate()'s `ev.querySelector('.release-country')` scope on this class, so without it the derived 'Release country' column is never built and the 'Country details - Name'/'- Code' sections vanish — the second half of what the bespoke shape lost.

name: the country <abbr> is no longer wrapped in its area anchor
why: EXPECTED TO PASS, recorded so the anchor is not mistaken for load-bearing. ColumnDataExtractor.splitCountryDate() rebuilds the anchor itself — `countryHref` falls back to '#' and the visible text comes from the <abbr>'s title and textContent — so the derived column still reads 'Name (XX)' inside an <a> either way. The anchor is kept for fidelity with native markup (and so area-decorating userscripts see a link), not because any assertion depends on it.

name: a dateless event emits no empty .release-date
why: Removes the date half of the alignment padding. splitCountryDate() pushes one <li> into its Date output per `.release-date`, so an event with a country and NO date contributes none and the two derived columns drift apart in a multi-event cell. Seen only by the DATELESS-row test — the countryless-row test stays green, which is why both exist.
grep: dateless event keeps its row aligned

name: a countryless event emits no empty .release-country
why: The mirror of the previous mutation: an event with a date and no country contributes no <li> to the Country column.
grep: country-less event keeps its row aligned

name: _rePopulateCell appends instead of replacing
why: Restores the unguarded `cell.appendChild(ul)` this function shipped with. Two passes can reach one cell before either stamps data-re-done, appending a SECOND <ul> so every event renders twice, in the cell and in both derived columns. WS/2 latency hides it live; a stubbed fetch reproduces it every time, which is how the spec found it.
grep: country-less event keeps its row aligned

name: 'Release events' is dropped from the hasFlagIcons name gate
why: hasFlagIcons is a column-NAME whitelist that deliberately excluded this column. Without the name, flagIconMap is never built and no entry gets a flag even though the markup now supports it — the half of the fix the shape change alone does not deliver.

name: iconSel stops excluding a flag with a third-party img inside it
why: EXPECTED TO PASS. Reverting this alone leaves the hollowed span matching iconSel again, but _bakeFlagIconNode() then returns null for it — it carries data-hq-processed and has no paintable visual — so no second segment is emitted. See the combined mutation below, which removes BOTH and does fail: that is what shows the pair is load-bearing rather than the spec proving nothing. The selector is kept because it is cheaper (no bake at all) and matches the precedent set by the wrapper-shape exclusion.

name: a neutralized flag is baked as a class-only clone again
why: EXPECTED TO PASS, and the symmetric half of the entry above. Removing the bake's null return alone changes nothing on this shape, because iconSel excludes the hollowed span before _bakeFlagIconNode() is ever reached. Neither guard is individually visible to this spec; the combined mutation below is what pins them. This one still earns its place: it is the guard that acts on any FUTURE shape the selector does not anticipate, which is precisely the case no fixture can be written for in advance.

name: baked flag clones no longer opt out of third-party re-decoration
why: Removes the data-hq-skip marker. RSFE's own rule `.flag:not([data-hq-processed]):not([data-hq-skip])` blanks such a clone with !important — beating our normal-priority inline background — and its MutationObserver then decorates it, inside a panel appended to document.body.
grep: bare class the userscript can repaint

name: BOTH hollow-flag guards removed together
why: The load-bearing one. iconSel and _bakeFlagIconNode()'s null return each cover for the other on this shape, so removing either alone leaves the spec green — recorded individually above. Removing both restores the original defect exactly: the Italy entry renders ['span','img'], the hollowed sprite AND the real image, one before the name and one after. If this mutation ever starts passing, the double-flag guarantee has no coverage at all, whatever the two entries above say.

name: the country flag goes back into the leading marker slot
why: Restores `marker.className = glyphClass` for the country kinds, putting the real flag back where the generic glyph belongs. The same decision was made once already for 'name' entries — which used to render '[flag] » area name: Spain' and now render '[glyph] » area name: Spain [flag]' — and the country kinds were never brought along, so one panel showed both conventions at once. Fails on 'leading slot keeps a generic glyph' rather than on 'the flag is NOT in the leading slot' — the marker becomes `flag flag-US`, so the missing generic glyph is what trips first. Both assertions cover the same relocation.

name: the country kinds emit no trailing flag
why: The other half: without `_trailingFlagClass` the country entries render a generic glyph and no flag at all, rather than moving it. Pins that the flag was RELOCATED and not merely removed from the leading slot — a mutation on the marker alone cannot tell those two outcomes apart.

name: the stylesheet no longer spaces the date off the country
why: Removes the rule that separates a release event's date from its country. A flag userscript's image sets margin-right 0.05em INLINE with !important, which no stylesheet rule can outrank, so the gap has to go on .release-date instead — and without it the cell reads "US<flag>2005-12-20". Affects MusicBrainz's own Country/Date column as well as this injected one; both carry the same markup.
grep: separated, in the cell AND the dropdown

name: the date spacing stops skipping a countryless event
why: Drops the :not(.no-country) qualifier, so a date with no country is spaced off an EMPTY span and simply indented. Seen only by the not-indented test; the main spacing test stays green, which is why both exist.

name: dropdown segments lose the space after a release-country flag
why: Clears spaceAfter. The panel rebuilds an entry as [text][cloned icon][text] with no separator between segments, so splitting the run at the flag loses the join that would have spaced the date — and the stylesheet cannot help, because the panel never clones the .release-date element. Scoped to a flag inside a .release-country precisely so an area chain, where the icon decorates the text that FOLLOWS it, keeps its flags tight against their names.
grep: separated, in the cell AND the dropdown

name: country NAME entries get no flag map
why: Stops populating countryNameFlagMap. A "Country" cell renders both halves of one value — "United States (US)" — so both dropdown sections describe the same flagged entity, but only the code half ever had a map. Fails on the Name section while the Code section stays green, which is what shows the two are wired independently.

name: the native Country/Date markup loses its date spacing
why: Narrows the stylesheet rule to this script's own injected cells, so MusicBrainz's native <li class="release-event"> no longer matches. The defect was reported against artist-releases' own Country/Date column and the spec pins the selector against that page's exact bytes, so a rule covering only the injected column must fail.
